conventions.convention: Assume Countable Choice. Spatial dimension d belongs to {1,2,3}; Q_d = ℝ^d/(2πℤ)^d carries probability measure (2π)^(-d) dx. Fourier coefficients use exp(-ik·x), and H^0 is the real coefficient completion identified with L² classes.

The number of modes r is at least one. Modes are real smooth periodic divergence-free fields orthonormal for the normalized L² inner product. A_ij integrates ∇v_j:∇v_i; c_ijk integrates ((v_j·∇)v_k)·v_i. The ODE has convection and νA terms on the left, with ν ≥ 0.
Solutions on [0,T) use a right derivative at zero, continuous extension of the derivative to zero, and no condition at the excluded endpoint T.
The global existence and energy conclusions concern only the specified finite coefficient ODE; no infinite-dimensional PDE existence, uniqueness, or Galerkin convergence follows.
The shear mode is v₁(x₁,x₂) = √2 sin(x₂)(1,0) on the normalized 2π-periodic torus; reduced energy is E(t) = a(t)²/2.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming Countable Choice, for d ∈ {1,2,3}, r ≥ 1, a finite smooth periodic divergence-free normalized-L²-orthonormal family, ν ≥ 0, and a⁰ ∈ ℝ^r, define A_ij = ∫∇v_j:∇v_i dμ and c_ijk = ∫((v_j·∇)v_k)·v_i dμ. The coefficient initial-value system is a_i′ + Σ_jk c_ijk a_j a_k + νΣ_j A_ij a_j = 0, with a_i(0) = a_i⁰.

Under the stated Countable Choice, dimension, finite smooth solenoidal orthonormal-family, ν ≥ 0, and initial-vector hypotheses, the specified coefficient system has exactly one solution a ∈ C¹([0,∞),ℝ^r). For every t ≥ 0, (1/2)(d/dt)|a(t)|² + ν∫|∇u_a(t)|² dμ = 0 and |a(t)|² + 2ν∫₀ᵗ∫|∇u_a(s)|² dμ ds = |a⁰|². These are finite-ODE conclusions only.

published_dependencies.used_for: Exact inherited assumption that every sequence of nonempty sets admits a choice function.
The Fourier-space supplier's probability Borel measure and finite-product torus conventions, rescaled by x = 2πy.
The Fourier-space supplier's normalized integral coefficients, characters, and finite trigonometric polynomials.
Under Countable Choice, the Fourier-space supplier's L² realization, Parseval identity, and surjective coefficient isometry.
Scalar completeness in the Fourier-space supplier's weighted coefficient-completion argument; its Statement was inspected.
The Picard–Lindelöf supplier's time-state domain and interval-solution conventions, including one-sided endpoint derivatives.
The exact compact-cylinder, locally uniform-in-time Lipschitz hypothesis verified for the polynomial autonomous lift.

Local existence and overlap uniqueness on the open domain ℝ × ℝ^r, including local existence at a proposed finite endpoint. Global continuation is proved locally rather than attributed to this supplier.
Convergence of the explicit Cauchy sequence a(t_n) at a proposed finite endpoint; the supplier's n ≥ 1 hypothesis is satisfied by r ≥ 1.
